title: RLM: Recursive Language Models for Large Codebases - Shashi, Superagentic AI
talk_summary: Shashi presents the MIT RLM (Recursive Language Models) pattern: instead of stuffing a large repo into a model's context, the model writes code in a sandboxed REPL to inspect/slice the repo, gets bounded observations back, and can recursively call sub-LLM queries for hard sub-questions, returning a synthesized answer. The talk is mostly a demo of their open-source 'RLM code' harness (Docker sandbox, budget/step/depth caps, JSONL traces) rather than new measured results.

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat the repo as data in a sandboxed execution environment; the model writes code to grep/slice/compute relevant chunks and only the bounded observations enter the main context window.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to externalize the context management into programmable execution environment

takeaways.technique: Recursive sub-LLM queries for hard sub-questions
takeaways.what_they_do: When the REPL loop needs info it can't cheaply extract, it issues an 'llm_query' to another model instance (one or many questions) and folds the answer back into the loop, terminating on a final synthesis.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the recussion part here is engineer ask another specialist using LLM query

takeaways.what_they_do: The harness takes an explicit budget plus max steps and recursion depth, and the run terminates when hit; traces record token usage per run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we specify the budget so that we don't not spending too much uh on this run

takeaways.technique: Docker sandbox per RLM run with JSONL traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Each run spins a fresh Docker container for the REPL; every run/session emits JSONL traces (REPL code, observations, sub-calls, tokens) importable into any observability tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're using the docker as a sandbox ... the docker container has been just started for this RLM

takeaways.what_they_do: The harness records the full trajectory (planning, REPL code, observations, sub-calls, final output) so a reviewer can inspect how a conclusion was reached, not just the answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that should capture the whole trajectory all these things like the planning coding observation sub call budget and the final output
